name: css-image-stacking

frames.best_why: Two photos are visibly pinned as a stack, the wide brick building above and the next picture arriving below it.

tagline: Building photos pin and pile up, each one a little wider than the last.
summary: A dark page of architectural photographs that pin in place as you scroll, each new picture settling over the previous one at a slightly larger width until six images have gathered into a stack.
appearance: Full-height photos of buildings, centred on a near-black page with rounded corners, growing from about half the width to four fifths. Earlier pictures stay pinned behind the newest one with a thin dark gap along the top.
behaviour: Scrolling pins each photo section at the top of the viewport so the next picture glides up over it while being a little wider. The pile builds with every section and then the last photo leaves with the page.
demo_content: Photos of a red brick tower, a grey apartment block, a brown brick building and a glass high-rise.
search_phrases: photos stack on top of each other on scroll
full screen pictures that pile up
pictures growing wider as you scroll
scroll page with overlapping picture cards
use_when: A photography page wants big images to gather into a stack as the reader scrolls.
avoid_when: Six screens of scroll carry six pictures, all with empty alt text and fixed percentage widths.
customise: No props: the six photo links and their width classes are written section by section in the file, and the heading and footer copy are fixed too.
weight_why: Six large remote photos load up front; the stacking itself is plain CSS sticky.

a11y.note: Every photo has empty alt text, so the stack conveys nothing to screen readers, and smooth scrolling ignores reduced-motion.

issues: All six photos have empty alt text and no captions.
Fixed percentage widths crop the buildings hard in tall or narrow windows.
Six full screens of scrolling carry six pictures with no text or context.
polish_why: Crisp large photos and a rhythmic stack; no captions and a bare, text-free sequence.
title: CSS Image Stacking
